_comment: A map recipe (#331, decision 0010): the land before anything is placed on it. size: the square map's side in metres, centred on the origin. relief: metres from the lowest to the highest the noise reaches. hill_mask: a slow noise (frequency, 1 / metres) whose value between from and to fades hilly country in; outside it lies near-flat lowland. layers: noise summed for the height, each with frequency, amplitude (share of relief), octaves, and masked (only where the hill mask says hilly, and only rising out of the lowland). coast (#454): the map is an island in the sea: sea_level metres, with open sea at least edge metres wide round the map; the coastline runs radius metres out from the middle (measured with the roundness power: 2 a circle, higher squarer), wobbled in and out by noise (frequency, amplitude metres, octaves) into bays and headlands; within inland metres of it lowland settles towards a beach rise metres over the sea, and hills keep their height until cliff.inland metres from it, then come down towards a cliff top cliff.rise over it (half to one and a half times that, varying along the coast); and across the shore the ground falls to sea_depth under the sea over sea_band metres seaward and land_band landward of the line, wide on a beach (beach), narrow under a cliff (cliff, where the hill mask is between from and to); sand on ground gentler than beach.sand_grade up to beach.sand_height metres over the sea, and on any ground short of rock (biomes.rock_grade_from to rock_grade_to) up to beach.wash metres over it, so no grass runs down to the water; bare rock where the shore is steep; islets rise rise metres out of the sea between near and far metres off the coastline where their noise (frequency) passes threshold; land the main island's ground does not reach is an islet zone, never used. walkable: max_grade (rise per metre a player still walks easily), min_share (the least share of the map that gentle), flat_grade and min_flat_share (near-flat ground for towns and fields, and how much of it the map needs), hillside_grade and min_hillside_share (real hillsides: the least share of the map that rises at least this much); the tests hold every seed to these. water: ponds where water would collect: the land is surveyed every cell metres, a basin at least min_depth deep and min_area square metres becomes a pond (shrunk to max_area by lowering its level), its level freeboard metres below where it would spill, its bed deepen times deeper than the land. biomes: noise fields for forest, dry grass and rock (frequency 1 / metres, threshold where a field starts), then shaped by the land: rock shows on ground steeper than rock_grade_from, fully past rock_grade_to, in patches rock_patch_frequency (1 / metres) apart; woods grow on the hills (hill_forest of the way) and in a few broad woodland regions (woodland_frequency, at most lowland_forest), the forest field cutting clearings into them; none in water. map_metres_per_texel: the terrain shader's biome map resolution. zones: the land classified every cell metres into water, wetland (within wet_distance of water), slope (steeper than slope_grade), hilltop (hilltop_rise metres above the ground hilltop_ring metres round it), forest (woods above forest_cutoff), flat (under flat_grade) and open (the rest); touching cells of a kind make a zone. uses: per use, the kinds it may go on and the smallest area (square metres) it needs. spawn_margin and spawn_edge: the player camp's spot, between this many metres from the map's edge (on an island, from the sea). settlements: the city's footprint is the largest square of its zone's cells, at least city.size metres, cut down to city.max_size in its middle (the size the city module builds, modules/city/data/city.json `size`); up to town.max towns, at least town.size, town.spacing metres from the city and each other; the camp stays camp.clearance metres outside them, on a level square pad camp.size metres a side (the fence and everything in the camp stand on it, see world.json camp) that the highway leaves from its side nearest the city; every settlement stays edge_margin metres in from the map's edge. On an island the camp stands camp.sea [nearest, furthest] metres from the sea, and a harbour spot is kept on the shore within harbour.reach metres of it: the ground at the waterline no steeper than max_grade, a jetty straight out to sea length [shortest, longest] metres long reaching min_depth metres of water over open sea, and size metres round its root kept free of roads, sites, power and trees. roads: the kinds (highway and two_lane between settlements, track from each site to the nearest road or track by the shortest way, always cut and filled, never bridged or tunnelled; width in metres, max_grade the steepest rise per metre they climb) and how the router weighs the land: cost is extra per metre on forest, slope, wetland and hilltop ground, over_grade per unit of grade beyond a kind's limit, settlement for passing through another settlement; a kind's cross_slope is extra per metre per unit of the land's slope across the way (a way along a hillside needs a notch cut and winds into switchbacks), and a track's legs that come back within its width of each other are joined; corners are rounded into arcs of each kind's min_radius metres (smaller where the straights are short), and the road is sampled every sample metres. Each road's height follows the land smoothed over profile_window metres (a kind may set its own: a track follows the land closely), held to its kind's max_grade; where it would cut deeper than max_cut it becomes a tunnel, where it would stand higher than max_fill above the land a bridge. earthworks: the land shaped by the roads and settlements: each road's width plus shoulder metres either side is cut or filled to the road's height, each settlement's footprint (plus shoulder) to its level, with banks rising bank_grade per metre (0.7 is about 35 degrees) out to where they meet the land, at most reach metres out (a track's banks rise track_bank_grade per metre, at most track_reach out); tunnels and bridges leave the land alone. remoteness: how far a place is from people, 0 to 1: the way from the nearest settlement or the camp, counting metres along a road once and off_road times over open land (water cannot be crossed); reach metres of way makes 1. sites: what stands out in the land, placed after the roads (#429): clearance metres kept free round roads, settlement_clearance round settlements, edge_margin in from the map's edge, spacing_any between any two sites; per kind in kinds, tried in this order, count [least, most], the zone kinds it may stand on, its remoteness [low, high], road: [nearest, furthest] metres from a road, spacing: metres from another of its kind, size: its footprint [x, z] in metres, max_grade: the steepest ground it stands on, prefer_high: try the highest spots first, min_height: the least share of the map's height range it stands at, and near / near_distance: within that many metres of a kind placed before it, or of a town's or the city's edge ('town'); max_track: the longest track the kind may have, in metres (a spot whose straight way to a road is too far for it is passed over, and a site whose track still runs longer is dropped). power: the lines placed last (#494), every foot at least edge_margin metres in from the map's edge and camp_clearance from the camp; where two lines cross, one's lowest wire must clear the other's highest by crossing_clearance metres. poles (placed first): wooden poles span [shortest, longest] metres apart beside the roads and tracks from a town or the city to up to count sites of the kinds in sites (the nearest along the roads first, no further than max_length metres), setback metres off the road's edge and never nearer than min_setback, on ground no steeper than max_grade; a pole line that comes within a span of an earlier one ends on one of its poles, leaving at least branch_angle degrees off that line. high_voltage: a fenced substation yard yard metres a side, substation [nearest, furthest] metres out from the city's edge, on ground rising at most yard_rise across it; a line from a terminal of its own in the yard (terminal_inset metres in from its fence, terminal_gap metres apart) to each town (the nearest towns first, at most towns of them), ending town_reach metres out from the town's edge, lattice pylons span [shortest, longest] metres apart, each foot foot metres round and keep_clear metres off roads, settlements, sites and other lines, on ground no steeper than max_grade; the route turns at most max_turn degrees at a pylon and is the cheapest by its length, turn_cost metres a degree turned and tower_cost metres a pylon. For both, the lowest wire hangs wire_height metres and the highest top_height over each foot (kept at least what the towers in modules/power/data/power.json give, the tests hold them to it), dips sag of a span's length at its middle, and must clear the ground by clearance metres all along.
